introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question. Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

In SECTION A, question 1 is compulsory in the following sense: answer either 1A* or 1B* (the two Starred questions) and one other question from the section.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION A: CAMEROON SINCE 1850**

Question one is compulsory. Answer either 1A* or 1B* and one other Question from this section.

**1. Or**

**B\*** (Starred question) Study this extract on the decolonisation of French Cameroon and then answer questions (a) to (e) which follow. (The maximum mark for each sub question is indicated in brackets)

> The 1939-45 War strongly influenced the growth of nationalism and decolonisation in so many ways
> during the Trusteeship period in French Cameroon. It saw the rise of so many political parties, trade unions and
> removal of harsh colonial policies from the French status books. The French started allowing freedom of
> association and other freedoms in the spirit of the Atlantic Charter of 1941, to allow the locals to govern
> themselves.
> The first indigenous political party in French Cameroon was created in the late 1940s. Amongst the [margin: 5]
> aims of the party was the reunification of French and British Cameroon. Because this party was allied to the
> French Communist party, it performed poorly in the 1951-52 elections that offered room for the locals to
> participate in the running of their affairs. In December 1952, the party presented a memorandum to the UN
> Visiting Mission in Cameron in which they highlighted their disgust with the French policies. They were [margin: 10]
> invited to present their case to the 4th Committee of the United Nations.
> In the 1950s the French colonial government took steps to check the influence of this party in the
> political affairs of French Cameroon. Their members were removed and refused to participate in local elections
> thereafter. A guerrilla war ensued in the Bassa and Bamileke regions. The French colonial administration
> promulgated the **Loi Cadre**, to prepare the territory towards self government. Elections into ALCAM were [margin: 15]
> held and the following results were produced:

| Political Party | No. of seats |
|---|---|
| Union Camerounais | 30 |
| Democrat Camerounais | 20 |
| Paysan Independents | 09 |
| Group D'Action Nationale | 08 |
| Independent Candidates | 03 |

> Between 1957 and 1959, when the Trusteeship Agreement with France and the United Nations ended,
> the transformation from a self-governing territory to an independent nation was rapid. Ahidjo and the French
> seemed to have worked so closely, which made it possible for French Cameroon to gain its independence.

**Source:** Adapted from *The Anglo-French Condominium in Cameroon 1914-1916: History of a misunderstanding* by Lovett Elango and edited by Panel.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a)
(i) What name is given to the 1939-45 war, mentioned in *line 1*?
(ii) Name any **one** trade union that was formed in French Cameroon before 1945 *(line 3)*.
(iii) Write down **two** harsh colonial policies that were removed from the French status books *(line 3)*.
(iv) In what year did the Trusteeship period begin in French Cameroon?

(1+1+2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)(i)** The 1939-45 war is called the **Second World War** (World War II). **[1 mark]**

**(a)(ii)** One trade union formed before 1945 is the **Union des Syndicats Confédérés du Cameroun (USCC)**, set up in Douala in **1944** (affiliated to the French CGT), after a decree of August 1944 had allowed African workers to form unions. **[1 mark]**

**(a)(iii)** Two harsh colonial policies removed from the French status books (in 1945-46):

- the **indigenat** (the native code, which allowed administrators to punish Africans without trial);
- **forced labour** (compulsory unpaid work on roads, railways and plantations), abolished by the law of 11 April 1946. (Compulsory cultivation of crops is another accepted answer.) **[2 marks]**

**(a)(iv)** The Trusteeship period began in **1946**, when the United Nations approved the Trusteeship Agreement for French Cameroon (13 December 1946) and replaced the League of Nations Mandate. **[the printed marks 1+1+2 total 4 marks for these four parts]**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b)
(i) Give the name and the year, the first indigenous party mentioned in *line 6* was formed in French Cameroon.
(ii) Apart from the reunification of the French and British Cameroon, give **two** other aims of the party in b(i) above.

(2 + 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i)** The party is the **Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC)**, founded in **1948** (10 April 1948, in Douala) under Ruben Um Nyobè (secretary-general), Félix Moumié, Ernest Ouandié and others. **[2 marks: name 1, year 1]**

**(b)(ii)** Two other aims of the UPC:

1. **Independence** for Cameroon: the end of French trusteeship and colonial rule, with a fixed date for independence. **[2 marks for two aims, 1 each]**
2. **Social justice and national development**: an end to forced labour and the abuses of the colonial administration, the improvement of living conditions, education and equality of rights for Cameroonians (also: national unity of the people.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c)
(i) Name the personality who presented the grievances of the party to the UN Visiting Mission of 1952 *(line 9)*.
(ii) Name any two of the grievances he presented to the UN Visiting Mission.
(iii) Name the French colonial administrator who took steps to check the influence of this party in French Cameroon *(line 12)*.

(1+2+1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(c)(i)** The personality was **Ruben Um Nyobè**, secretary-general of the UPC (known as "Mpodol", the spokesman). He also went to New York in December 1952 to address the Fourth Committee of the United Nations. **[1 mark]**

**(c)(ii)** Any two grievances presented by Um Nyobè and the UPC:

- the **lack of a date for reunification and independence** (the French treated the territory as part of the French Union instead of preparing it for self-government); **[1 mark]**
- **electoral fraud and unfair elections** and the denial of political freedoms to the party; **[1 mark]**
- also accepted: abuses of the colonial administration (forced labour, police harassment, repression of UPC militants) and the economic and social injustices of French rule.

**(c)(iii)** The French High Commissioner who tried to check the UPC was **Roland Pré** (High Commissioner from 1950 to 1954). (Pierre Messmer, High Commissioner from 1956, is also associated with the later war against the UPC.) **[1 mark]**
themes: upc and french repression in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d)
(i) From the results recorded in the ALCAM election, write down the names of any of the **two** political parties that formed the first internal self-government in 1957.
(ii) Name the head of the first self-government in French Cameroon.

(2 + 1 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(d)(i)** From the table, the two parties that formed the first internal self-government (1957) were the **Union Camerounaise (UC)** of Ahidjo, with 30 seats, and the **Démocrates Camerounais (DC)** of Mbida, with 20 seats (together 50 of the 70 seats; the other three groups had 9, 8 and 3). **[2 marks]**

**(d)(ii)** The head of the first self-government was **André-Marie Mbida**, Prime Minister from May 1957 (with Ahidjo as Deputy Prime Minister). **[1 mark]**

*Check of the table.* 30 + 20 + 9 + 8 + 3 = 70 seats.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(e)
(i) In what year did Ahidjo gain independence for French Cameroon?
(ii) What activities did he carry out to consolidate his hold on power before 1970?

(1 + 3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(e)(i)** Independence was gained on **1 January 1960**, i.e. in **1960** (Ahidjo, Prime Minister since February 1958, became the first President in May 1960). **[1 mark]**

**(e)(ii)** Activities Ahidjo carried out to consolidate his hold on power before 1970 (any three well explained, 1 mark each):

1. **A strong presidential constitution** (1960) giving the President large powers, and the 1961 federation, in which he became President of the Federal Republic.
2. **Crushing the UPC rebellion** with the French army (guerrilla war in the Bamileke and Bassa regions) and the **trial and execution of rebel leaders** (Ernest Ouandié was executed in January 1971).
3. **Restricting opposition**: from the early 1960s he used ordinances on subversion and on the press and public meetings, and **banned or absorbed opposition parties** until all were merged into the single party, the **Cameroon National Union (CNU/UNC) in 1966**.
4. **Control of the Anglophone region**: he used the Federal government and the CNU to reduce the autonomy of West Cameroon.
5. **Patronage and regional balance** in appointments, and the use of the security services to monitor opponents.
